import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations

This file states the finite-time singularity problem for smooth, finite-energy solutions of the
three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on `ℝ³`. It also states Elgindi's finite-time
singularity theorem at lower Hölder regularity.

## References

- [Wikipedia, Euler equations (fluid dynamics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_equations_%28fluid_dynamics%29)
- [T. M. Elgindi, *Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions to the
  incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R^3$*](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2021.194.3.2)
-/

namespace EulerEquations

open ContDiff Filter InnerProductSpace MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology

private abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- The divergence of a vector field on `ℝ³`. -/
noncomputable def divergence (v : Space → Space) (x : Space) : ℝ :=
  (fderiv ℝ v x).trace ℝ Space

/-- The curl of a vector field on `ℝ³`. -/
noncomputable def curl (v : Space → Space) (x : Space) : Space :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 ![
    (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)) 2 -
      (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1)) 1,
    (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1)) 0 -
      (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1)) 2,
    (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1)) 1 -
      (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)) 0]

/-- The pointwise supremum norm, valued in `ℝ≥0∞` so that it can equal infinity. -/
noncomputable def supremumNorm {E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] (v : Space → E) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ x, ENNReal.ofReal ‖v x‖

/-- The incompressible Euler equations on a set of times. -/
def IsEulerSolutionOn (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (p : Space → ℝ → ℝ)
    (f : Space → ℝ → Space) (times : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x t, t ∈ times → DifferentiableAt ℝ (p · t) x) ∧
  (∀ x t, t ∈ times →
    derivWithin (u x) times t + fderiv ℝ (u · t) x (u x t) + gradient (p · t) x = f x t) ∧
  ∀ x t, t ∈ times → divergence (u · t) x = 0

/-- Finite kinetic energy and the forced Euler energy balance on a set of times. -/
def HasFiniteEnergyBalanceOn (u f : Space → ℝ → Space) (times : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ t ∈ times,
    MemLp (u · t) 2 ∧
    Integrable (fun x ↦ Inner.inner ℝ (u x t) (f x t)) ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s ↦ ∫ x, ‖u x s‖ ^ 2)
      (2 * ∫ x, Inner.inner ℝ (u x t) (f x t)) times t

/-- A bounded $C^{1,\alpha}$ function on all of its domain. -/
def IsCOneHolder {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : ℝ≥0) (v : E → F) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 1 v ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (range v) ∧
    Bornology.IsBounded (range (fderiv ℝ v)) ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ≥0, HolderWith C α (fderiv ℝ v)

/-- A bounded $C^{1,\alpha}$ function on a subset of its domain. -/
def IsCOneHolderOn {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : ℝ≥0) (v : E → F) (s : Set E) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ 1 v s ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (v '' s) ∧
    Bornology.IsBounded (fderivWithin ℝ v s '' s) ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ≥0, HolderOnWith C α (fderivWithin ℝ v s) s

/-- A spacetime field is $C^{1,\alpha}$ up to every time strictly before `T`. -/
def IsCOneHolderBefore (α : ℝ≥0) (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 ≤ τ → τ < T →
    IsCOneHolderOn α (Function.uncurry u) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 τ)

/-- Reflection of one coordinate of a point in `ℝ³`. -/
def reflectCoordinate (x : Space) (i : Fin 3) : Space :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update (WithLp.ofLp x) i (-x i))

/-- Each component is odd in its matching coordinate and even in the other two coordinates. -/
def IsOddVelocity (u : Space → Space) : Prop :=
  (∀ i x, u (reflectCoordinate x i) i = -u x i) ∧
  ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x, u (reflectCoordinate x j) i = u x i

/--
Can a smooth, divergence-free, finite-energy solution of the forced three-dimensional
incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R^3\times[0,T)$ form a singularity in finite time?
Precisely, the force is smooth and square-integrable on $\mathbb R^3\times[0,T]$, the solution
satisfies the energy balance, and the pointwise spatial supremum of $\lVert\nabla u\rVert$ tends
to infinity as $t\to T^-$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 35]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ T : ℝ, 0 < T ∧ ∃ u : Space → ℝ → Space, ∃ p : Space → ℝ → ℝ,
        ∃ f : Space → ℝ → Space,
          ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
          ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry p) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
          ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry f) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T) ∧
          MemLp (Function.uncurry f) 2 (volume.restrict (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T)) ∧
          IsEulerSolutionOn u p f (Ico 0 T) ∧
          HasFiniteEnergyBalanceOn u f (Ico 0 T) ∧
          Tendsto (fun t ↦ supremumNorm (fun x ↦ fderiv ℝ (u · t) x)) (𝓝[<] T) atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Elgindi's solved lower-regularity variant: there are $\alpha>0$ and divergence-free, odd initial
data $u_0\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb R^3)$ whose vorticity obeys
$|\omega_0(x)|\le C/(|x|^\alpha+1)$, such that the unique odd, unforced
$C^{1,\alpha}_{x,t}$ Euler solution on $[0,1)$ satisfies
$\int_0^t\|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds\to+\infty$ as $t\to1^-$. These solutions have infinite
energy and do not satisfy the finite-energy balance in `euler_equations`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 35]
theorem euler_equations.variants.elgindi :
    ∃ α : ℝ≥0, 0 < α ∧ ∃ u₀ : Space → Space,
      IsCOneHolder α u₀ ∧
      (∀ x, divergence u₀ x = 0) ∧
      IsOddVelocity u₀ ∧
      (∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x,
        ‖curl u₀ x‖ ≤ C / (‖x‖ ^ (α : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      ∃ u : Space → ℝ → Space, ∃ p : Space → ℝ → ℝ,
        IsEulerSolutionOn u p (0 : Space → ℝ → Space) (Ico 0 1) ∧
        (∀ x, u x 0 = u₀ x) ∧
        (∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, IsOddVelocity (u · t)) ∧
        IsCOneHolderBefore α u 1 ∧
        (∀ v : Space → ℝ → Space,
          ((∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, IsOddVelocity (v · t)) ∧
            IsCOneHolderBefore α v 1 ∧
            (∃ q : Space → ℝ → ℝ,
              IsEulerSolutionOn v q (0 : Space → ℝ → Space) (Ico 0 1) ∧
              ∀ x, v x 0 = u₀ x)) → v = u) ∧
        Tendsto (fun t ↦ ∫⁻ s in Ioc 0 t, supremumNorm (curl (u · s))) (𝓝[<] (1 : ℝ)) atTop := by
  sorry

end EulerEquations
modeling_decisions: The terse list entry is interpreted, following the background article and Elgindi's Question 1.1, as the finite-time blow-up question for the forced three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on ℝ³ rather than on a torus or for the compressible equations.

The primary question uses a positive lifespan T, a smooth velocity and pressure on ℝ³ × [0,T), and a smooth spacetime-L² force on ℝ³ × [0,T]. Finite energy is required at every pre-blow-up time, and the energy-balance derivative is required together with integrability of the work term.

Pointwise spatial suprema are represented in ℝ≥0∞ by an indexed supremum of norm values. Thus tending to `atTop` faithfully represents divergence to +∞ without assigning a junk real supremum to an unbounded field. The Jacobian carries the operator norm; in finite dimensions its blow-up is equivalent to blow-up in the usual matrix norms.

Elgindi's `C^{1,α}` norm is modeled by bounded function and derivative, continuous differentiability, and an α-Hölder derivative. For the solution on [0,1), this condition is imposed on every truncated interval [0,τ] with τ<1, allowing the norms to diverge at the blow-up time.
Elgindi's oddness is modeled componentwise: component i is odd in coordinate i and even in each other coordinate, rather than merely requiring u(-x)=-u(x).

Uniqueness in Elgindi's result is uniqueness of the velocity among odd unforced C^{1,α} solutions with the given initial data. Pressure is existential for each candidate because pressure itself is only unique up to a time-dependent additive gauge.

The primary declaration is tagged `research open` and uses `answer(sorry)` because it is a yes/no question. Elgindi's established subordinate result is tagged `research solved` and stated positively with a `sorry` proof body.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations

This file states the finite-time singularity question for smooth, finite-energy solutions of the
three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$. It also states Elgindi's solved
$C^{1,\alpha}$, infinite-energy variant.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Euler equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_equations_%28fluid_dynamics%29)
- [T. M. Elgindi, *Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions to the
  incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal Topology

namespace EulerEquations

abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
abbrev Velocity := Space → ℝ → Space
abbrev Pressure := Space → ℝ → ℝ

/-- The spatial Fréchet derivative (velocity gradient) of a time-dependent vector field. -/
noncomputable def spatialDerivative (u : Velocity) (x : Space) (t : ℝ) : Space →L[ℝ] Space :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun y ↦ u y t) x

/-- The spatial Fréchet derivative of a time-independent vector field. -/
noncomputable def jacobian (u : Space → Space) (x : Space) : Space →L[ℝ] Space :=
  fderiv ℝ u x

/-- The divergence of a time-independent vector field on $\mathbb{R}^3$. -/
noncomputable def divergence (u : Space → Space) (x : Space) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin 3, jacobian u x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) i

/-- The curl of a time-independent vector field on $\mathbb{R}^3$. -/
noncomputable def curl (u : Space → Space) (x : Space) : Space :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 ![jacobian u x (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1) 2 -
      jacobian u x (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1) 1,
    jacobian u x (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1) 0 -
      jacobian u x (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) 2,
    jacobian u x (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) 1 -
      jacobian u x (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1) 0]

/-- The vorticity $\nabla\times u$ at a given time. -/
noncomputable def vorticity (u : Velocity) (x : Space) (t : ℝ) : Space :=
  curl (fun y ↦ u y t) x

/-- The supremum norm of the vorticity, valued in $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\cup\{\infty\}$. -/
noncomputable def vorticitySup (u : Velocity) (t : ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  ⨆ x : Space, ‖vorticity u x t‖₊

/-- The reflection which changes the sign of coordinate `i`. -/
noncomputable def reflectCoordinate (i : Fin 3) (x : Space) : Space :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update (WithLp.ofLp x) i (-x i))

/-- A velocity field is odd on `I` when its `i`th component is odd in `xᵢ` and its other
components are even in `xᵢ`, for each `i` and each time in `I`. -/
def IsOddOn (u : Velocity) (I : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Fin 3) (x : Space) (t : ℝ), t ∈ I →
    u (reflectCoordinate i x) t = reflectCoordinate i (u x t)

/-- The global $C^{1,\alpha}$ condition used here: the function is $C^1$ and its Fréchet derivative
 is $\alpha$-Hölder. -/
def IsC1Alpha {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : ℝ≥0) (g : E → F) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ ∃ C : ℝ≥0, HolderWith C α (fderiv ℝ g)

/-- The $C^{1,\alpha}$ condition on a set. -/
def IsC1AlphaOn {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : ℝ≥0) (g : E → F) (s : Set E) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g s ∧ ∃ C : ℝ≥0, HolderOnWith C α (fderiv ℝ g) s

/-- The momentum and incompressibility equations on a time interval. -/
def SolvesEulerOn (u : Velocity) (p : Pressure) (f : Velocity) (I : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x t, t ∈ I →
    fderiv ℝ (u x) t 1 + spatialDerivative u x t (u x t) +
      gradient (fun y ↦ p y t) x = f x t) ∧
  ∀ x t, t ∈ I → divergence (fun y ↦ u y t) x = 0

/-- The kinetic-energy balance for a finite-energy velocity field and force. -/
def HasEnergyBalanceOn (u f : Velocity) (I : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ t ∈ I, MemLp (fun x ↦ u x t) 2) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ I, HasDerivWithinAt (fun s ↦ ∫ x, ‖u x s‖ ^ 2) (2 * ∫ x, inner ℝ (u x t) (f x t)) I t

/-- Blow-up of the spatial velocity gradient as time approaches `T` from below. -/
def HasGradientBlowupAt (u : Velocity) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Tendsto (fun t ↦ ⨆ x : Space, ENNReal.ofNNReal ‖spatialDerivative u x t‖₊)
    (𝓝[<] T) atTop

/-- Divergence of the time integral of the vorticity supremum as time approaches `T` from below. -/
def HasVorticityIntegralBlowupAt (u : Velocity) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Tendsto (fun t ↦ ∫⁻ s in Ioc 0 t, vorticitySup u s) (𝓝[<] T) atTop

/--
**Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations.** Fixing the standard whole-space formulation,
does there exist a finite time $T>0$, a smooth velocity $u$ and pressure $p$ on
$\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,T)$, and a smooth $L^2$ force on $\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,T]$, such that
$\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=f$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, the finite-energy balance
holds, and $\sup_x|\nabla u(x,t)|\to+\infty$ as $t\to T^-$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (T : ℝ) (u : Velocity) (p : Pressure) (f : Velocity),
      0 < T ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ ⊤ (Function.uncurry u) (Set.univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ ⊤ (Function.uncurry p) (Set.univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ ⊤ (Function.uncurry f) (Set.univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T) ∧
      MemLp (Function.uncurry f) 2 (volume.restrict (Set.univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T)) ∧
      SolvesEulerOn u p f (Ico 0 T) ∧ HasEnergyBalanceOn u f (Ico 0 T) ∧
      HasGradientBlowupAt u T := by
  sorry

/--
**Elgindi's $C^{1,\alpha}$ finite-time singularity theorem.** There are $\alpha>0$ and a
divergence-free odd datum $u_0\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ whose vorticity obeys
$|\omega_0(x)|\leq C/(|x|^\alpha+1)$, such that the unique odd $C^{1,\alpha}$ solution of the
unforced incompressible Euler equations on $[0,1)$ has initial datum $u_0$ and satisfies
$\int_0^t\|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds\to+\infty$ as $t\to1^-$. These solutions have infinite
energy and do not satisfy the energy balance in `euler_equations`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations.variants.elgindi :
    ∃ (α : ℝ≥0) (u₀ : Space → Space) (u : Velocity) (p : Pressure),
      0 < α ∧ IsC1Alpha α u₀ ∧ (∀ x, divergence u₀ x = 0) ∧
      (∀ i x, u₀ (reflectCoordinate i x) = reflectCoordinate i (u₀ x)) ∧
      (∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x, ‖curl u₀ x‖ ≤ C / (‖x‖ ^ (α : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      IsC1AlphaOn α (Function.uncurry u) (Set.univ ×ˢ Ico 0 1) ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry p) (Set.univ ×ˢ Ico 0 1) ∧
      IsOddOn u (Ico 0 1) ∧ SolvesEulerOn u p (fun _ _ ↦ 0) (Ico 0 1) ∧
      (∀ x, u x 0 = u₀ x) ∧
      (∀ (v : Velocity) (q : Pressure),
        IsC1AlphaOn α (Function.uncurry v) (Set.univ ×ˢ Ico 0 1) →
        ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry q) (Set.univ ×ˢ Ico 0 1) →
        IsOddOn v (Ico 0 1) → SolvesEulerOn v q (fun _ _ ↦ 0) (Ico 0 1) →

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations

The incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ describe the motion of an ideal fluid
with velocity $u(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$, pressure $p(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}$ and external
force $f(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$:
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0.$$

Whether smooth, finite-energy solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Euler
equations can form a singularity in finite time is a major open problem. This file
formalizes the question in the form given by Elgindi (Question 1.1 of the reference
below), and the special case of $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions, for which finite-time
singularity formation was established by Elgindi (Main Theorem of the reference below).

## Conventions

The velocity is encoded as `u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³`, so that `u x t` is the velocity at position
`x` and time `t`; similarly for the pressure `p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ` and the force
`f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³`. The values of these functions outside the time interval of the problem
are irrelevant. Since the problem is posed on the time interval $[0,T)$, time derivatives
are encoded with `derivWithin` relative to `Set.Ico 0 T`, and smoothness on
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$ with `ContDiffOn`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Euler equations (fluid dynamics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_equations_%28fluid_dynamics%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [T. M. Elgindi, *Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions to the
  incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$*, Ann. of Math. 194 (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)
-/

open ContDiff Set InnerProductSpace MeasureTheory EuclideanGeometry Filter Topology
open scoped NNReal

namespace EulerEquations

/--
The divergence $\nabla \cdot v = \sum_i \partial_i v_i$ of a vector field
$v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ at a point $x$, computed as the trace of the Jacobian.
If `v` is not differentiable at `x`, then `fderiv` is the zero map and the divergence is `0`.
-/
noncomputable def divergence (v : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (x : ℝ³) : ℝ := (fderiv ℝ v x).trace ℝ ℝ³

/--
The curl (vorticity) $\nabla \times v$ of a vector field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$
at a point $x$:
$$\nabla \times v = (\partial_2 v_3 - \partial_3 v_2,\ \partial_3 v_1 - \partial_1 v_3,\
\partial_1 v_2 - \partial_2 v_1).$$
If `v` is not differentiable at `x`, then `fderiv` is the zero map and the curl is `0`.
-/
noncomputable def curl (v : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (x : ℝ³) : ℝ³ :=
  let D : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ := fun i j => fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) j
  !₂[D 1 2 - D 2 1, D 2 0 - D 0 2, D 0 1 - D 1 0]

/-- The divergence of the zero vector field is zero. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem divergence_zero (x : ℝ³) : divergence 0 x = 0 := by
  simp [divergence]

/-- The divergence is the sum of the partial derivatives $\sum_i \partial_i v_i$. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem divergence_eq_sum (v : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (x : ℝ³) :
    divergence v x = ∑ i, fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) i := by
  rw [divergence, LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace ℝ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℝ).toBasis]
  simp [Matrix.trace, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]

/-- The curl of a constant vector field is zero. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem curl_const (c x : ℝ³) : curl (fun _ => c) x = 0 := by
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;> simp [curl]

/-- The rotation field $(x_1, x_2, x_3) \mapsto (-x_2, x_1, 0)$, as a continuous linear map. -/
noncomputable def rotationField : ℝ³ →L[ℝ] ℝ³ :=
  -(EuclideanSpace.proj 1).smulRight (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) +
    (EuclideanSpace.proj 0).smulRight (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)

/-- The curl of the rotation field $(-x_2, x_1, 0)$ is $(0, 0, 2)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem curl_rotationField (x : ℝ³) : curl rotationField x = !₂[0, 0, 2] := by
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;> simp [curl, rotationField, EuclideanSpace.single_apply]
  norm_num

/--
A pair `(u, p)` is a solution of the incompressible Euler equations with external force `f`
on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$:
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0.$$
The pressure is required to be differentiable in space so that $\nabla p$ is genuine.
Regularity requirements on `u` are imposed separately.
-/
structure IsEulerSolution (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) :
    Prop where
  /-- The Euler equation $\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f$
  on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$. -/
  euler : ∀ x, ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T,
    derivWithin (u x ·) (Ico 0 T) t + fderiv ℝ (u · t) x (u x t) + gradient (p · t) x = f x t
  /-- Incompressibility $\nabla \cdot u = 0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$. -/
  div_free : ∀ x, ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, divergence (u · t) x = 0
  /-- The pressure is differentiable in space at each time $t \in [0,T)$. -/
  pressure_differentiable : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, Differentiable ℝ (p · t)

/--
An external force `f` in the class $(C^\infty \cap L^2)(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T])$ of
Elgindi's Question 1.1: `f` is smooth on the closed slab $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T]$, all its
space-time derivatives are bounded there, and $f(\cdot, t) \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for every
$t \in [0,T]$.

Uniform boundedness of the derivatives makes precise the requirement that the force is
smooth *up to and including* the time $T$; without it, a force whose derivatives are
unbounded at spatial infinity can drive a trivial singularity that escapes to infinity.
-/
structure IsSmoothForce (T : ℝ) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  /-- The force is smooth on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T]$. -/
  smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿f) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T)
  /-- Every space-time derivative of the force is bounded on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T]$. -/
  bounded_derivs : ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ q ∈ univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T,
    ‖iteratedFDerivWithin ℝ m (↿f) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T) q‖ ≤ M
  /-- The force is square-integrable in space at each time $t \in [0,T]$. -/
  memLp : ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T, MemLp (f · t) 2

/--
A smooth finite-energy solution `(u, p)` of the Euler equations with force `f` on
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$, in the sense of Elgindi's Question 1.1:
- `u` is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$;
- `u` has finite kinetic energy, $u(\cdot, t) \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for $t \in [0,T)$;
- the energy balance
  $$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u(x,t)|^2\,dx = 2 \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} u(x,t) \cdot f(x,t)\,dx$$
  holds for all $t \in [0,T)$;
- `u` is a classical solution before time `T`: $\sup_x |\nabla u(x,t)| < \infty$ for each
  $t \in [0,T)$.
-/
structure IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop extends IsEulerSolution T u p f where
  /-- The velocity is smooth on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$. -/
  smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T)
  /-- The velocity has finite kinetic energy at each time $t \in [0,T)$. -/
  finite_energy : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, MemLp (u · t) 2
  /-- The energy balance $\frac{d}{dt} \int |u|^2\,dx = 2 \int u \cdot f\,dx$ for
  $t \in [0,T)$. -/
  energy_balance : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T,
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s => ∫ x, ‖u x s‖ ^ 2) (2 * ∫ x, ⟪u x t, f x t⟫_ℝ) (Ico 0 T) t
  /-- The velocity gradient is bounded in space at each time $t \in [0,T)$. -/
  gradient_bounded : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, BddAbove (range fun x => ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖)

/--
**Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations.** Can a smooth, finite-energy solution of
the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations form a singularity in finite time?

Precisely (Elgindi, Question 1.1): given $T > 0$, an external force
$f \in (C^\infty \cap L^2)(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T])$, and a solution
$u \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T))$ of
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0$$
satisfying the energy balance
$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u|^2\,dx = 2 \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} u \cdot f\,dx$ on $[0,T)$,
is it possible that
$$\lim_{t \to T} \sup_{x} |\nabla u(x,t)| = +\infty?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³),
      0 < T ∧ IsSmoothForce T f ∧ IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution T u p f ∧
        Tendsto (fun t => ⨆ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖) (𝓝[<] T) atTop := by
  sorry

/-- The reflection $x \mapsto (x_1, \dots, -x_i, \dots, x_3)$ of the `i`-th coordinate. -/
noncomputable def reflectCoord (i : Fin 3) (x : ℝ³) : ℝ³ :=
  x - (2 * x i) • EuclideanSpace.single i 1

/-- Reflecting the `i`-th coordinate negates the `i`-th coordinate. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem reflectCoord_apply_self (i : Fin 3) (x : ℝ³) : reflectCoord i x i = -x i := by
  simp [reflectCoord]; ring

/-- Reflecting the `i`-th coordinate fixes the other coordinates. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem reflectCoord_apply_of_ne {i j : Fin 3} (h : j ≠ i) (x : ℝ³) :
    reflectCoord i x j = x j := by
  simp [reflectCoord, EuclideanSpace.single_apply, h]

/--
A vector field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is **odd** (Elgindi, Definition 1.1) if
$v_i$ is odd in $x_i$ and even in the other two variables, for each $1 \le i \le 3$.
Equivalently, `v` commutes with each coordinate reflection.
-/
def IsOdd (v : ℝ³ → ℝ³) : Prop := ∀ i x, v (reflectCoord i x) = reflectCoord i (v x)

/-- The zero vector field is odd. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem isOdd_zero : IsOdd 0 := by
  intro i x
  simp [reflectCoord]

/--
A vector field $v$ belongs to $C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ (in the sense of Elgindi's
Section 1.5): `v` is $C^1$ and $\nabla v$ is bounded and $\alpha$-Hölder continuous.
-/
def IsC1Holder (α : ℝ≥0) (v : ℝ³ → ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 1 v ∧ ∃ C : ℝ≥0, HolderWith C α (fderiv ℝ v) ∧ ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ v x‖ ≤ C

/--
A pair `(u, p)` is an odd solution of the incompressible Euler equations without external
force ($f \equiv 0$) on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,1)$, with initial velocity `u₀`, in the class
$C^{1,\alpha}_{x,t}([0,1) \times \mathbb{R}^3)$ of classical solutions: `u` is $C^1$ in
space-time on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,1)$ and, for every $T < 1$,
$u(\cdot, t) \in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ uniformly for $t \in [0,T]$.

The velocity itself is not required to be bounded or to decay: the solutions of Elgindi's
theorem have infinite energy.
-/
structure IsOddHolderEulerSolution (α : ℝ≥0) (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³)
    (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop extends IsEulerSolution 1 u p 0 where
  /-- The initial condition $u(\cdot, 0) = u_0$. -/
  initial_condition : ∀ x, u x 0 = u₀ x
  /-- The velocity is odd at each time $t \in [0,1)$. -/
  odd : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 1, IsOdd (u · t)
  /-- The velocity is $C^1$ in space-time on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,1)$. -/
  contDiffOn : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (↿u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 1)
  /-- For each $T < 1$, the spatial gradient of the velocity is bounded and
  $\alpha$-Hölder continuous on $\mathbb{R}^3$, uniformly for $t \in [0,T]$. -/
  holder : ∀ T ∈ Ico 0 1, ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T,
    HolderWith C α (fderiv ℝ (u · t)) ∧ ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖ ≤ C

$$\lim_{t \to 1} \int_0^t \|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds = +\infty,$$
where $\omega = \nabla \times u$ is the vorticity.

The solution is stated to exist; its uniqueness (Lichtenstein, Gunther) is not encoded.
These solutions have infinite energy, so this is a lower-regularity special case of
`euler_equations` and does not answer that question.

modeling_decisions: Primary slot follows Elgindi (arXiv:1904.04795) Question 1.1 verbatim as the precise form of the terse list entry: domain ℝ³ (not the torus), external force allowed, finite energy encoded as u(·,t) ∈ L² for t ∈ [0,T) plus the energy balance d/dt ∫|u|² dx = 2∫ u·f dx (as `HasDerivWithinAt` on `Ico 0 T`), blow-up quantity sup_x|∇u(x,t)| (operator norm of `fderiv`), not the equivalent BKM vorticity integral.

The solution class for the open question requires sup_x|∇u(x,t)| < ∞ for every t < T (`gradient_bounded`), i.e. the solution is classical before T. Without this, the real-valued `⨆` is junk 0, and with an ℝ≥0∞-valued sup the answer would be trivially 'yes': a stationary sum of shrinking, far-apart divergence-free bumps (amplitude 1, radius 2^{-k}) is smooth, in L², satisfies the energy balance with f = u·∇u ∈ C^∞ ∩ L², and has unbounded gradient at every time. Reviewers should confirm they accept this reading of 'singularity formation at time T'.

Force class `IsSmoothForce`: Elgindi's 'f ∈ (C^∞ ∩ L²)(ℝ³ × [0,T])' is read as: ContDiffOn ∞ on the closed slab ℝ³×[0,T], all space-time derivatives uniformly bounded on that slab, and f(·,t) ∈ L²(ℝ³) for each t ∈ [0,T]. The uniform bound is an added precision: with only pointwise smoothness, a trivial 'yes' exists (bumps u_k of radius 2^{-k} at x_k → ∞ switched on by cutoffs a_k(t) supported in [T−2^{-k},T] give u smooth on ℝ³×[0,T), finite energy, bounded gradient for t<T, gradient → ∞, and f := ∂_t u + u·∇u pointwise smooth on ℝ³×[0,T] and L²). L² is taken per time slice rather than space-time L² so that the energy balance integrand u·f is integrable.

Pressure: only spatial differentiability of p(·,t) is required (to make `gradient` genuine, not junk 0). For a smooth u the normalized pressure is automatically smooth, so this does not restrict the class; Elgindi's question imposes nothing on p.

Time derivative is `derivWithin (u x ·) (Ico 0 T) t` and smoothness is `ContDiffOn` on `univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T`, matching the half-open time interval [0,T) of the source (the Navier–Stokes file uses the same idiom with `Ici 0`).

Elgindi variant: 'the unique local odd solution … satisfies' is rendered as ∃ (u,p) in the class with blow-up; uniqueness is NOT asserted. Reason: in the formal class odd linear flows u = A(t)x (A diagonal, traceless, A(0)=0, quadratic pressure) are C^{1,α} solutions with zero data, so a ∀-solutions form could be false while the theorem is true; the ∃ form is exactly what is constructed.

Class C^{1,α}_{x,t}([0,1)×ℝ³) is rendered as: u is C¹ jointly on ℝ³×[0,1), and for every T<1, u(·,t) ∈ C^{1,α}(ℝ³) (bounded, α-Hölder spatial gradient) uniformly for t ∈ [0,T]. It is deliberately NOT a uniform space-time Hölder class: Elgindi's self-similar solutions have u ~ |x|^{1−α} and hence unbounded ∂_t u, so a uniform space-time C^{1,α} requirement would make the statement false. Also local-in-time uniformity is required since the solution blows up at t=1. Following Elgindi's Section 1.5, C^{1,α} does not require u itself to be bounded (his solutions have infinite energy).
Oddness (Elgindi Def. 1.1: u_i odd in x_i, even in the other variables) is encoded as u ∘ σ_i = σ_i ∘ u for each coordinate reflection σ_i (`reflectCoord`); this is equivalent.
α is quantified as `α : ℝ≥0` with `0 < α` (no upper bound), matching 'there exists α > 0'; `HolderWith` with α > 1 forces a constant gradient and cannot yield blow-up, so no spurious witnesses arise.
Blow-up quantity in the variant is `∫ s in 0..t, ⨆ x, ‖curl (u · s) x‖` tending to atTop along 𝓝[<] 1; the sup is a genuine real since the class bounds the spatial gradient on [0,t] for t<1.

Vorticity is the bespoke `curl` (components ∂₂v₃−∂₃v₂, ∂₃v₁−∂₁v₃, ∂₁v₂−∂₂v₁ via `fderiv`); its sign convention is unit-tested on the rotation field (−x₂,x₁,0) ↦ (0,0,2). Divergence is the trace of `fderiv`, with an API lemma showing it equals Σ_i ∂_i v_i.

/--
**Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations.** Can a smooth, finite-energy solution of
the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations form a singularity in finite time?

Precisely (Elgindi, Question 1.1): given $T > 0$, an external force
$f \in (C^\infty \cap L^2)(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T])$, and a solution
$u \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T))$ of
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0$$
satisfying the energy balance
$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u|^2\,dx = 2 \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} u \cdot f\,dx$ on $[0,T)$,
is it possible that
$$\lim_{t \to T} \sup_{x} |\nabla u(x,t)| = +\infty?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³),
      0 < T ∧ IsSmoothForce T f ∧ IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution T u p f ∧
        Tendsto (fun t => ⨆ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖) (𝓝[<] T) atTop := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions** (Elgindi, Main Theorem).
There exist $\alpha > 0$ and a divergence-free, odd $u_0 \in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ whose
initial vorticity satisfies $|\omega_0(x)| \le \frac{C}{|x|^\alpha + 1}$ for some constant
$C > 0$, such that the (unique) local odd solution of the Euler equations with $f \equiv 0$
and initial velocity $u_0$ in the class $C^{1,\alpha}_{x,t}([0,1) \times \mathbb{R}^3)$
satisfies
$$\lim_{t \to 1} \int_0^t \|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds = +\infty,$$
where $\omega = \nabla \times u$ is the vorticity.

The solution is stated to exist; its uniqueness (Lichtenstein, Gunther) is not encoded.
These solutions have infinite energy, so this is a lower-regularity special case of
`euler_equations` and does not answer that question.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations.variants.elgindi :
    ∃ (α : ℝ≥0) (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³), 0 < α ∧ IsC1Holder α u₀ ∧ (∀ x, divergence u₀ x = 0) ∧
      IsOdd u₀ ∧ (∃ C > 0, ∀ x, ‖curl u₀ x‖ ≤ C / (‖x‖ ^ (α : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      ∃ (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), IsOddHolderEulerSolution α u₀ u p ∧
        Tendsto (fun t => ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..t, ⨆ x, ‖curl (u · s) x‖) (𝓝[<] 1) atTop := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations

The incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for a velocity field $u(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$
and a pressure $p(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}$ are
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0.$$

Wikipedia lists "Regularity of solutions of Euler equations" as an unsolved problem: whether
solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations can form a singularity in finite
time. We follow the precise formulation of Elgindi (Question 1.1 of
[arXiv:1904.04795](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)): can a smooth, finite-energy solution
$u$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,T)$ satisfy $\lim_{t \to T} \sup_x |\nabla u(x,t)| = +\infty$?
We also state Elgindi's main theorem, which answers the analogous question positively for the
lower regularity class $C^{1,\alpha}$.

## Conventions

The velocity is `u : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ^3` and the pressure is `p : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ`, so that `u x t`
is the velocity at position `x` and time `t`. Solutions live on the time interval `Ico 0 T`, and
the time derivative is `derivWithin` relative to `Ico 0 T`, which is one-sided at `t = 0`.
The term $(u \cdot \nabla) u$ is the spatial derivative of `u` applied to `u`, and the divergence
is the trace of the spatial derivative. We consider the free equations (no external force), as in
the Wikipedia article; Elgindi's question also allows a smooth square-integrable force.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Euler equations (fluid dynamics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_equations_%28fluid_dynamics%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- T. M. Elgindi, *Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions to the
  incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$*, Ann. of Math. (2) 194 (2021), 647–727.
  [arXiv:1904.04795](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)
-/

open ContDiff EuclideanGeometry Filter MeasureTheory Set Topology
open scoped NNReal

namespace EulerEquations

/-- The divergence $\nabla \cdot v = \sum_i \partial_i v_i$ of a vector field
$v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ at a point $x$, computed as the trace of the Jacobian.
If `v` is not differentiable at `x`, then `fderiv` is the zero map and the divergence is `0`. -/
noncomputable def divergence (v : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3) (x : ℝ^3) : ℝ :=
  (fderiv ℝ v x).trace ℝ (ℝ^3)

/-- The divergence of the zero vector field is zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem divergence_zero (x : ℝ^3) : divergence 0 x = 0 := by
  simp [divergence]

/-- The divergence of a constant vector field is zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem divergence_const (c x : ℝ^3) : divergence (fun _ => c) x = 0 := by
  simp [divergence]

/-- The divergence is `0` at points where `fderiv` has its junk value. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem divergence_of_not_differentiableAt {v : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3} {x : ℝ^3}
    (hv : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℝ v x) : divergence v x = 0 := by
  simp [divergence, fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hv]

/-- The curl $\nabla \times v$ of a vector field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ at a
point $x$, with components $\partial_2 v_3 - \partial_3 v_2$, $\partial_3 v_1 - \partial_1 v_3$
and $\partial_1 v_2 - \partial_2 v_1$. Here $\partial_j v_i$ is the `i`-th component of
`fderiv ℝ v x` applied to the `j`-th standard basis vector. The curl of the velocity field of a
fluid is its vorticity.
If `v` is not differentiable at `x`, then `fderiv` is the zero map and the curl is `0`. -/
noncomputable def curl (v : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3) (x : ℝ^3) : ℝ^3 :=
  let D : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ := fun j i => fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single j 1) i
  !₂[D 1 2 - D 2 1, D 2 0 - D 0 2, D 0 1 - D 1 0]

/-- The curl of the zero vector field is zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem curl_zero (x : ℝ^3) : curl 0 x = 0 := by
  simp [curl]

/-- The curl of a constant vector field is zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem curl_const (c x : ℝ^3) : curl (fun _ => c) x = 0 := by
  simp [curl]

/-- The curl is `0` at points where `fderiv` has its junk value. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem curl_of_not_differentiableAt {v : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3} {x : ℝ^3}
    (hv : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℝ v x) : curl v x = 0 := by
  simp [curl, fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hv]

/-- The shear flow $v(x) = (x_2, 0, 0)$ has constant vorticity $\nabla \times v = (0, 0, -1)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem curl_shear (x : ℝ^3) :
    curl (fun y => (EuclideanSpace.proj (1 : Fin 3)).smulRight (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 : ℝ^3) y)
      x = !₂[0, 0, -1] := by
  simp only [curl, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv]
  simp [EuclideanSpace.single_apply]

/-- A vector field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is **odd** (in the sense of Elgindi,
Definition 1.2) if for each $i$ the component $v_i$ is odd in the variable $x_i$ and even in the
other two variables. Here `x - (2 * x j) • EuclideanSpace.single j 1` is the reflection of `x`
that changes the sign of the `j`-th coordinate. -/
def IsOdd (v : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : ℝ^3) (i j : Fin 3),
    v (x - (2 * x j) • EuclideanSpace.single j 1) i = if i = j then -v x i else v x i

/-- The zero vector field is odd. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem isOdd_zero : IsOdd 0 := by
  intro x i j
  simp

/-- The identity vector field $x \mapsto x$ is odd. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem isOdd_id : IsOdd id := by
  intro x i j
  by_cases h : i = j
  · subst h
    simp
    ring
  · simp [h, EuclideanSpace.single_apply]

/-- A non-zero constant vector field is not odd. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem not_isOdd_const {c : ℝ^3} (hc : c ≠ 0) : ¬ IsOdd (fun _ => c) := by
  intro h
  apply hc
  ext i
  have := h 0 i i
  simp only [if_true] at this
  simp only [WithLp.ofLp_zero, Pi.zero_apply]
  linarith

/-- A vector field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ with constant
`C` if it is continuously differentiable and its derivative $\nabla v$ is bounded by `C` and
$\alpha$-Hölder continuous with constant `C`. Following Elgindi, no bound on `v` itself is
imposed, so `v` may be unbounded. -/
def IsC1HolderWith (C α : ℝ≥0) (v : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 1 v ∧ (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ v x‖ ≤ C) ∧ HolderWith C α (fderiv ℝ v)

/-- A vector field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ if it is
continuously differentiable and its derivative $\nabla v$ is bounded and $\alpha$-Hölder
continuous. -/
def IsC1Holder (α : ℝ≥0) (v : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3) : Prop :=
  ∃ C, IsC1HolderWith C α v

/-- A constant vector field is of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ with constant `0` for every $\alpha$. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem isC1HolderWith_const (α : ℝ≥0) (c : ℝ^3) : IsC1HolderWith 0 α (fun _ => c) :=
  ⟨contDiff_const, fun x => by simp, fun x y => by simp⟩

/-- A constant vector field is of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ for every $\alpha$. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem isC1Holder_const (α : ℝ≥0) (c : ℝ^3) : IsC1Holder α (fun _ => c) :=
  ⟨0, isC1HolderWith_const α c⟩

/-- A pair `(u, p)` of a velocity field and a pressure solves the incompressible Euler equations
without external force on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$:
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0.$$
The time derivative is taken within `Ico 0 T`, so it is one-sided at `t = 0`. -/
structure IsEulerSolution (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ^3) (p : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where
  /-- The Euler momentum equation $\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = 0$. -/
  euler : ∀ x, ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T,
    derivWithin (u x ·) (Ico 0 T) t + fderiv ℝ (u · t) x (u x t) + gradient (p · t) x = 0
  /-- The incompressibility constraint $\nabla \cdot u = 0$. -/
  div_free : ∀ x, ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, divergence (u · t) x = 0

/-- The fluid at rest solves the Euler equations. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem isEulerSolution_zero (T : ℝ) : IsEulerSolution T 0 0 where
  euler x t _ := by simp
  div_free x t _ := by simp [divergence]

/-- A smooth, finite-energy solution `(u, p)` of the incompressible Euler equations on
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$, in the sense of Question 1.1 of Elgindi's paper (with $f = 0$):
- `u` and `p` are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$;
- `u` has finite kinetic energy, $u(\cdot, t) \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for every $t \in [0, T)$;
- the energy balance $\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u(x,t)|^2 \, dx = 0$ holds, which we
  state in integrated form as conservation of energy;
- for each time $t < T$, the gradient $\nabla u(\cdot, t)$ is bounded on $\mathbb{R}^3$, so
  that the solution is regular before time $T$ and a blow-up of $\sup_x |\nabla u(x,t)|$ as
  $t \to T$ is a genuine loss of regularity at time $T$. -/
structure IsSmoothFiniteEnergyEulerSolution (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ^3) (p : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ) :
    Prop extends IsEulerSolution T u p where
  /-- The velocity is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$. -/
  velocity_smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T)
  /-- The pressure is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$. -/
  pressure_smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿p) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T)
  /-- The velocity is square-integrable at each time $t \in [0, T)$ (finite energy). -/
  memLp : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, MemLp (u · t) 2
  /-- The kinetic energy is conserved: $\int |u(x,t)|^2 \, dx = \int |u(x,0)|^2 \, dx$
  for all $t \in [0, T)$. -/
  energy_conservation : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, ∫ x, ‖u x t‖ ^ 2 = ∫ x, ‖u x 0‖ ^ 2
  /-- The gradient of the velocity is bounded on $\mathbb{R}^3$ at each time $t \in [0, T)$. -/
  gradient_bounded : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, BddAbove (range fun x => ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖)

/-- The fluid at rest is a smooth finite-energy solution of the Euler equations. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem isSmoothFiniteEnergyEulerSolution_zero (T : ℝ) :
    IsSmoothFiniteEnergyEulerSolution T 0 0 where
  toIsEulerSolution := isEulerSolution_zero T
  velocity_smooth := contDiffOn_const
  pressure_smooth := contDiffOn_const
  memLp t _ := by simp
  energy_conservation t _ := by simp
  gradient_bounded t _ := ⟨0, by rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩; simp⟩

/-- **Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations** (Wikipedia list entry), in the precise
form of Question 1.1 of Elgindi's paper, for the free equations ($f = 0$):

Is it possible that a $C^\infty$, divergence-free, finite-energy solution $u$ of the
three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$, satisfying the
energy balance and with $\nabla u(\cdot, t)$ bounded for each $t < T$, has
$$\lim_{t \to T} \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^3} |\nabla u(x,t)| = +\infty?$$

Here $|\nabla u(x,t)|$ is the operator norm of the spatial derivative `fderiv ℝ (u · t) x`.
A positive answer means finite-time singularity formation for smooth solutions; a negative
answer means global regularity. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ T > 0, ∃ (u : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ^3) (p : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ),
      IsSmoothFiniteEnergyEulerSolution T u p ∧
        Tendsto (fun t => ⨆ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖) (𝓝[<] T) atTop := by
  sorry

/-- A classical solution `(u, p)` of the incompressible Euler equations on
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$ of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ with initial velocity `u₀`:
- `u` is $C^1$ in space and time on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$ with `u x 0 = u₀ x`;
- on each time interval $[0, T']$ with $T' < T$, the spatial derivative $\nabla u(\cdot, t)$ is
  bounded and $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, uniformly in $t \in [0, T']$;
- the pressure $p(\cdot, t)$ is $C^1$ in space for every $t \in [0, T)$. -/
structure IsClassicalEulerSolution (α : ℝ≥0) (T : ℝ) (u₀ : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3) (u : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ^3)
    (p : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop extends IsEulerSolution T u p where
  /-- The initial condition $u(x, 0) = u_0(x)$. -/
  initial_condition : ∀ x, u x 0 = u₀ x
  /-- The velocity is $C^1$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$. -/
  velocity_contDiff : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (↿u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T)
  /-- The velocity is uniformly of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ in space on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T']$
  for every $T' < T$. -/
  velocity_holder : ∀ T' < T, ∃ C, ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T', IsC1HolderWith C α (u · t)
  /-- The pressure is $C^1$ in space at each time $t \in [0, T)$. -/
  pressure_contDiff : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, ContDiff ℝ 1 (p · t)

/-- The fluid at rest is a classical solution of the Euler equations with zero initial velocity. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem isClassicalEulerSolution_zero (α : ℝ≥0) (T : ℝ) : IsClassicalEulerSolution α T 0 0 0 where
  toIsEulerSolution := isEulerSolution_zero T
  initial_condition _ := rfl
  velocity_contDiff := contDiffOn_const
  velocity_holder _ _ := ⟨0, fun _ _ => isC1HolderWith_const α 0⟩
  pressure_contDiff _ _ := contDiff_const

/-- **Elgindi's theorem** (Main Theorem of [arXiv:1904.04795](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)):
finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions of the three-dimensional
incompressible Euler equations.

There exist $\alpha > 0$ and a divergence-free, odd initial velocity
$u_0 \in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ whose vorticity $\omega_0 = \nabla \times u_0$ satisfies
$|\omega_0(x)| \le C / (|x|^\alpha + 1)$ for some constant $C > 0$, such that the (unique)
odd classical solution of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, 1)$ with initial
velocity $u_0$ and no external force satisfies
$$\lim_{t \to 1} \int_0^t \|\omega(\cdot, s)\|_{L^\infty} \, ds = +\infty,$$
where $\omega = \nabla \times u$ is the vorticity of the solution.

This is a special case of the blow-up question `euler_equations` with the regularity $C^\infty$
replaced by $C^{1,\alpha}$; the solutions have infinite energy and do not satisfy the energy
balance, so the question for smooth finite-energy solutions remains open. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations.variants.elgindi :
    ∃ α : ℝ≥0, 0 < α ∧ ∃ u₀ : ℝ^3 → ℝ^3,
      IsC1Holder α u₀ ∧ (∀ x, divergence u₀ x = 0) ∧ IsOdd u₀ ∧
      (∃ C > 0, ∀ x, ‖curl u₀ x‖ ≤ C / (‖x‖ ^ (α : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      ∃ (u : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ^3) (p : ℝ^3 → ℝ → ℝ),
        IsClassicalEulerSolution α 1 u₀ u p ∧ (∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, IsOdd (u · t)) ∧
        Tendsto (fun t => ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..t, ⨆ x, ‖curl (u · s) x‖) (𝓝[<] 1) atTop := by
  sorry

end EulerEquations

import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Millenium.NavierStokes

/-!
# Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations

The list entry "Regularity of solutions of Euler equations" refers to the regularity and possible
finite-time singularity formation of solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Euler
equations
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0$$
on $\mathbb{R}^3$. We follow the precise formulation of Elgindi [El21, Question 1.1]: can a
$C^\infty$, divergence-free, finite-energy solution $u$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$, with
external force $f \in (C^\infty \cap L^2)(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T])$ and satisfying the energy
balance $\frac{d}{dt}\int |u|^2 = 2 \int u \cdot f$, have
$\lim_{t \to T} \sup_x |\nabla u(x, t)| = +\infty$?

The main theorem of [El21] answers the analogous question for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions
(with $\alpha > 0$ small) in the affirmative: there are odd, divergence-free
$C^{1,\alpha}$ initial data with decaying vorticity whose solution satisfies
$\lim_{t \to 1} \int_0^t \|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds = +\infty$. These solutions have infinite
energy, so this does not answer the primary question.

## Variable conventions

Velocity fields are written `u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³` in the curried order `u x t` (position before
time), as in the source and in `FormalConjectures.Millenium.NavierStokes`, from which we reuse the
divergence `∇⬝`. Since the time domain is the half-open interval $[0, T)$, time derivatives are
encoded with `derivWithin` relative to `Set.Ico 0 T`.

## References

- [Wikipedia, Euler equations (fluid dynamics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_equations_%28fluid_dynamics%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [El21] Elgindi, Tarek M. *Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions to the
  incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$*. Ann. of Math. (2) 194 (2021), no. 3, 647–727.
  [arXiv:1904.04795](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)
-/

open Set Filter Topology MeasureTheory InnerProductSpace EuclideanGeometry

namespace EulerEquations

/- ### Vector calculus on `ℝ³` -/

/--
The curl $\nabla \times v$ (vorticity) of a vector field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ at a
point $x$, computed from the Jacobian `fderiv ℝ v x`:
$$(\nabla \times v)_1 = \partial_2 v_3 - \partial_3 v_2, \quad
  (\nabla \times v)_2 = \partial_3 v_1 - \partial_1 v_3, \quad
  (\nabla \times v)_3 = \partial_1 v_2 - \partial_2 v_1.$$
If `v` is not differentiable at `x`, then `fderiv` is the zero map, so this definition has the
corresponding junk value $0$.
-/
noncomputable def curl (v : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (x : ℝ³) : ℝ³ :=
  -- `D j i` is the partial derivative $\partial_j v_i$ at `x`.
  let D : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ := fun j i => fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single j 1) i
  WithLp.toLp 2 ![D 1 2 - D 2 1, D 2 0 - D 0 2, D 0 1 - D 1 0]

/-- The curl of a vector field is $0$ at points where `fderiv` has its junk value. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem curl_of_not_differentiableAt {v : ℝ³ → ℝ³} {x : ℝ³}
    (hv : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℝ v x) : curl v x = 0 := by
  simp [curl, fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hv]

/-- The curl of a constant vector field is zero. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem curl_const (c : ℝ³) (x : ℝ³) : curl (fun _ : ℝ³ => c) x = 0 := by
  simp [curl]

/-- The curl of the identity vector field is zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 35]
theorem curl_id (x : ℝ³) : curl id x = 0 := by
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;> simp [curl, EuclideanSpace.single_apply]

/-- The rotation field $x \mapsto (-x_2, x_1, 0)$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, as a continuous linear map. -/
noncomputable def rotationField : ℝ³ →L[ℝ] ℝ³ :=
  (EuclideanSpace.proj 1).smulRight (-EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) +
    (EuclideanSpace.proj 0).smulRight (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)

/-- The rotation field is $x \mapsto (-x_2, x_1, 0)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem rotationField_apply (x : ℝ³) : rotationField x = WithLp.toLp 2 ![-x 1, x 0, 0] := by
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;> simp [rotationField, EuclideanSpace.single_apply]

/-- The curl of the rotation field $x \mapsto (-x_2, x_1, 0)$ is the constant vector $(0, 0, 2)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem curl_rotationField (x : ℝ³) : curl rotationField x = WithLp.toLp 2 ![0, 0, 2] := by
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;> simp [curl, rotationField, EuclideanSpace.single_apply]
  norm_num

/- ### Symmetry and regularity classes -/

/-- The reflection of `x : ℝ³` that changes the sign of the `i`-th coordinate. -/
def flipCoord (i : Fin 3) (x : ℝ³) : ℝ³ :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update (WithLp.ofLp x) i (-x i))

/-- The flipped coordinate changes sign. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem flipCoord_apply_self (i : Fin 3) (x : ℝ³) : flipCoord i x i = -x i := by
  simp [flipCoord]

/-- The other coordinates are unchanged. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem flipCoord_apply_of_ne {i j : Fin 3} (h : j ≠ i) (x : ℝ³) : flipCoord i x j = x j := by
  simp [flipCoord, Function.update_of_ne h]

/-- Flipping a coordinate twice is the identity. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 35]
theorem flipCoord_flipCoord (i : Fin 3) (x : ℝ³) : flipCoord i (flipCoord i x) = x := by
  ext j
  by_cases h : j = i
  · subst h; simp
  · simp [h]

/--
A velocity field $v : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is **odd** (in the sense of
[El21, Definition 1.1]) if, for each $1 \le i \le 3$, the component $v_i$ is odd in $x_i$ and even
in the other two variables.
-/
structure IsOddVelocity (v : ℝ³ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  /-- $v_i$ is odd in the variable $x_i$. -/
  odd : ∀ i x, v (flipCoord i x) i = -v x i
  /-- $v_i$ is even in the variable $x_j$ for $j \ne i$. -/
  even : ∀ i j x, j ≠ i → v (flipCoord j x) i = v x i

/-- The zero velocity field is odd. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem isOddVelocity_zero : IsOddVelocity (0 : ℝ³ → ℝ³) := by
  constructor <;> simp

/-- The identity velocity field is odd. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem isOddVelocity_id : IsOddVelocity (id : ℝ³ → ℝ³) := by
  constructor
  · intro i x; simp
  · intro i j x h; simp [h.symm]

  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]

/--
A function $f$ is of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ on a set $s$, in the sense of [El21, Section 1.5]:
$f$ is $C^1$ on $s$ and its derivative $\nabla f$ (computed within $s$) is bounded and globally
$\alpha$-Hölder continuous on $s$. Note that $f$ itself is not required to be bounded.
-/
structure IsC1HolderOn (α : ℝ≥0) (f : E → F) (s : Set E) : Prop where
  /-- $f$ is continuously differentiable on $s$. -/
  contDiffOn : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f s
  /-- $\nabla f$ is bounded on $s$. -/
  bddAbove : BddAbove ((fun x => ‖fderivWithin ℝ f s x‖) '' s)
  /-- $\nabla f$ is $\alpha$-Hölder continuous on $s$. -/
  holder : ∃ C : ℝ≥0, HolderOnWith C α (fderivWithin ℝ f s) s

/-- A continuous linear map is of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ on the whole space. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem isC1HolderOn_clm (α : ℝ≥0) (L : E →L[ℝ] F) : IsC1HolderOn α L univ where
  contDiffOn := L.contDiff.contDiffOn
  bddAbove := ⟨‖L‖, by rintro _ ⟨x, -, rfl⟩; simp [L.fderiv]⟩
  holder := ⟨0, fun x _ y _ => by simp [L.fderiv]⟩

/- ### The incompressible Euler equations -/

/--
`IsEulerSolution T u p f` says that the velocity `u` and pressure `p` solve the incompressible Euler
equations with external force `f` on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$:
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0.$$
Here `u x t` is the velocity at position `x` and time `t`. The time derivative is taken within
$[0, T)$, so it is one-sided at $t = 0$.
-/
structure IsEulerSolution (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) :
    Prop where
  /-- The momentum equation $\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f$. -/
  euler : ∀ x, ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T,
    derivWithin (u x ·) (Ico 0 T) t + fderiv ℝ (u · t) x (u x t) + gradient (p · t) x = f x t
  /-- The incompressibility constraint $\nabla \cdot u = 0$. -/
  div_free : ∀ x, ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, ∇⬝ (u · t) x = 0
  /-- The pressure is differentiable in space, so that $\nabla p$ is meaningful. -/
  differentiable_pressure : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, Differentiable ℝ (p · t)

/-- A constant velocity field with zero pressure and zero force solves the Euler equations. -/
@[category test, AMS 35]
theorem isEulerSolution_const (T : ℝ) (c : ℝ³) :
    IsEulerSolution T (fun _ _ => c) (fun _ _ => 0) 0 where
  euler := by simp
  div_free := by simp
  differentiable_pressure := by simp

/--
The class of solutions considered in [El21, Question 1.1]: `u` is a $C^\infty$ solution of the
incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$ with pressure `p` and external force
`f`, where
* `u` and `p` are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$;
* `f` is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T]$ and belongs to $L^2$ (both on the space-time
  domain $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T]$, and on each time slice, so that $\int u \cdot f$ below is
  meaningful);
* `u` has finite energy, $u(\cdot, t) \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for all $t \in [0, T)$, and satisfies
  the energy balance
  $$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} |u(x, t)|^2\,dx
  = 2 \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} u(x, t) \cdot f(x, t)\,dx \qquad \text{for all } t \in [0, T);$$
* `u` is a classical solution before time $T$: $\nabla u$ is bounded on
  $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T']$ for every $T' < T$. This standard implicit hypothesis is needed so
  that a singularity at time $T$ is a genuine *formation* of a singularity; without it a solution
  that is singular (has unbounded gradient) at every time would count.
-/
structure IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop extends IsEulerSolution T u p f where
  /-- The velocity is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$. -/
  smooth_velocity : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T)
  /-- The pressure is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$. -/
  smooth_pressure : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿p) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T)
  /-- The force is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T]$. -/
  smooth_force : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (↿f) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T)
  /-- The force is in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T])$. -/
  memLp_force : MemLp (↿f) 2 (volume.restrict (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T))
  /-- The force is in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at each time $t \in [0, T]$. -/
  memLp_force_slice : ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T, MemLp (f · t) 2
  /-- The velocity has finite energy: $u(\cdot, t) \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for $t \in [0, T)$. -/
  memLp_velocity : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T, MemLp (u · t) 2
  /-- The energy balance $\frac{d}{dt}\int |u|^2\,dx = 2\int u \cdot f\,dx$ on $[0, T)$. -/
  energy_balance : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T,
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s => ∫ x, ‖u x s‖ ^ 2) (2 * ∫ x, ⟪u x t, f x t⟫_ℝ) (Ico 0 T) t
  /-- The solution is classical before time $T$: $\nabla u$ is bounded on
  $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T']$ for every $T' < T$. -/
  bddAbove_fderiv : ∀ T' < T, ∃ M, ∀ x, ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T', ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖ ≤ M

/--
**Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations** ([El21, Question 1.1]).

Is it possible that a $C^\infty$ solution $u$ of the three-dimensional incompressible Euler
equations
$$\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla) u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0$$
on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T)$, with external force
$f \in (C^\infty \cap L^2)(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T])$ and satisfying the energy balance
$\frac{d}{dt}\int |u|^2\,dx = 2\int u \cdot f\,dx$, forms a singularity in finite time, i.e.
$$\lim_{t \to T} \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^3} |\nabla u(x, t)| = +\infty?$$

The supremum is taken in $[0, \infty]$. The solution is assumed classical (with bounded gradient)
before time $T$, see `IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ) (f : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³),
      0 < T ∧ IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution T u p f ∧
      Tendsto (fun t => ⨆ x, (‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖₊ : ENNReal)) (𝓝[<] T) (𝓝 ⊤) := by
  sorry

/--
`IsHolderOddSolution α u₀ u` says that `u` is an odd solution of the incompressible Euler equations
without external force on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, 1)$ with initial data `u₀`, belonging to the
class $C^{1,\alpha}_{x,t}([0, 1) \times \mathbb{R}^3)$ of [El21, Theorem 1]: for every $T < 1$,
`u` is $C^{1,\alpha}$ in space and time on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T]$.
-/
structure IsHolderOddSolution (α : ℝ≥0) (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (u : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  /-- `u` solves the Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, 1)$ with $f \equiv 0$, for some
  pressure `p`. -/
  exists_pressure : ∃ p, IsEulerSolution 1 u p 0
  /-- The initial condition $u|_{t = 0} = u_0$. -/
  initial_condition : ∀ x, u x 0 = u₀ x
  /-- The velocity is odd at every time $t \in [0, 1)$. -/
  odd : ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 1, IsOddVelocity (u · t)
  /-- The velocity is $C^{1,\alpha}$ in space and time on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, T]$ for every
  $T < 1$. -/
  holder : ∀ T < 1, IsC1HolderOn α (↿u) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T)

/--
**Elgindi's theorem** ([El21, Theorem 1]): finite-time singularity formation for
$C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$.

There exist $\alpha > 0$ and a divergence-free, odd $u_0 \in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ with
initial vorticity $|\omega_0(x)| \le \frac{C}{|x|^\alpha + 1}$ for some constant $C > 0$, such that
the unique local odd solution to the Euler equations (with $f \equiv 0$) belonging to the class
$C^{1,\alpha}_{x,t}([0, 1) \times \mathbb{R}^3)$ satisfies
$$\lim_{t \to 1} \int_0^t \|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds = +\infty,$$
where $\omega = \nabla \times u$ is the vorticity and
$\|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty} = \sup_x |\omega(x, s)|$.

Here "the unique solution satisfies the blow-up" is rendered as: a solution in this class exists,
and every solution in this class satisfies the blow-up. These solutions have infinite energy and do
not satisfy the energy balance, so this is a special case at lower regularity and not an answer to
`euler_equations`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 35 76]
theorem euler_equations.variants.elgindi :
    ∃ (α : ℝ≥0) (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³), 0 < α ∧
      IsC1HolderOn α u₀ univ ∧ (∀ x, ∇⬝ u₀ x = 0) ∧ IsOddVelocity u₀ ∧
      (∃ C > 0, ∀ x, ‖curl u₀ x‖ ≤ C / (‖x‖ ^ (α : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      (∃ u, IsHolderOddSolution α u₀ u) ∧
      ∀ u, IsHolderOddSolution α u₀ u →
        Tendsto (fun t => ∫⁻ s in Ico 0 t, ⨆ x, (‖curl (u · s) x‖₊ : ENNReal)) (𝓝[<] 1) (𝓝 ⊤) := by
  sorry

end EulerEquations

This file states the finite-time singularity question for smooth, finite-energy solutions of the
three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on `ℝ³`. It also states Elgindi's solved
lower-regularity variant.

## References

- [Wikipedia, *Euler equations (fluid dynamics)*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_equations_%28fluid_dynamics%29)
- [T. M. Elgindi, *Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions to the
  incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R^3$](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)
-/

open Filter InnerProductSpace MeasureTheory Set Topology EuclideanGeometry

namespace EulerEquations

abbrev VelocityVector := ℝ^3

/-- The divergence of a vector field on `ℝ³`, defined as the trace of its derivative. -/
noncomputable def divergence (u : VelocityVector → VelocityVector) (x : VelocityVector) : ℝ :=
  (fderiv ℝ u x).trace ℝ VelocityVector

/-- The vorticity $\omega=\nabla\times u$ of a vector field on `ℝ³`. -/
noncomputable def vorticity (u : VelocityVector → VelocityVector) (x : VelocityVector) : VelocityVector :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 ![(fderiv ℝ u x (WithLp.toLp 2 (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1))) 2 -
      (fderiv ℝ u x (WithLp.toLp 2 (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1))) 1,
    (fderiv ℝ u x (WithLp.toLp 2 (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1))) 0 -
      (fderiv ℝ u x (WithLp.toLp 2 (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1))) 2,
    (fderiv ℝ u x (WithLp.toLp 2 (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1))) 1 -
      (fderiv ℝ u x (WithLp.toLp 2 (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1))) 0]

/-- The extended spatial supremum of the norm of the derivative of `u` at time `t`. -/
noncomputable def gradientSup (u : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector) (t : ℝ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ x, ENNReal.ofReal ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖

/-- The extended spatial $L^\infty$ norm of the vorticity of `u` at time `t`. -/
noncomputable def vorticitySup (u : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector) (t : ℝ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ x, ENNReal.ofReal ‖vorticity (u · t) x‖

/-- Elgindi's parity condition: $u_i$ is odd in $x_i$ and even in the other coordinates. -/
def IsOddVelocity (u : VelocityVector → VelocityVector) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : VelocityVector) (i j : Fin 3),
    u (WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j (-x.ofLp j))) i = if i = j then -u x i else u x i

/-- Global bounded $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity on a set. -/
def IsC1AlphaOn {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : ℝ≥0) (g : E → F) (s : Set E) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g s ∧
  Bornology.IsBounded (g '' s) ∧
  Bornology.IsBounded (fderivWithin ℝ g s '' s) ∧
  ∃ C : ℝ≥0, HolderOnWith C α (fderivWithin ℝ g s) s

/-- Local $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity on a set. The Hölder bound may depend on a neighborhood,
so it need not remain uniform when approaching a boundary point outside the set. -/
def IsLocallyC1AlphaOn {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : ℝ≥0) (g : E → F) (s : Set E) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g s ∧ ∀ z ∈ s, ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∃ r ∈ 𝓝[s] z,
    HolderOnWith C α (fderivWithin ℝ g s) (r ∩ s)

/-- A smooth solution of the forced incompressible Euler equations on
$\mathbb R^3\times[0,T)$ satisfying the kinetic-energy balance. -/
def IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution (T : ℝ) (u : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector)
    (p : VelocityVector → ℝ → ℝ) (f : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ (⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞) (Function.uncurry u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ (⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞) (Function.uncurry p) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
  (∀ x t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) T →
    derivWithin (u x) (Ico 0 T) t + fderiv ℝ (u · t) x (u x t) + gradient (p · t) x = f x t) ∧
  (∀ x t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) T → divergence (u · t) x = 0) ∧
  (∀ t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) T → MemLp (u · t) 2) ∧
  (∀ t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) T → Integrable (fun x ↦ ⟪u x t, f x t⟫_ℝ)) ∧
  (∀ t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) T →
    derivWithin (fun s ↦ ∫ x : VelocityVector, ‖u x s‖ ^ 2) (Ico 0 T) t =
      2 * ∫ x : VelocityVector, ⟪u x t, f x t⟫_ℝ)

/-- A $C^{1,\alpha}$ solution of the unforced incompressible Euler equations on
$\mathbb R^3\times[0,1)$ with initial velocity `u₀`. -/
def IsC1AlphaFreeSolution (α : ℝ≥0) (u₀ : VelocityVector → VelocityVector)
    (u : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector) (p : VelocityVector → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsLocallyC1AlphaOn α (Function.uncurry u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 1) ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry p) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 1) ∧
  (∀ x t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1 →
    derivWithin (u x) (Ico 0 1) t + fderiv ℝ (u · t) x (u x t) + gradient (p · t) x = 0) ∧
  (∀ x t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1 → divergence (u · t) x = 0) ∧
  (∀ x, u x 0 = u₀ x)

/--
Can a smooth, divergence-free, finite-energy solution of the forced three-dimensional
incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R^3\times[0,T)$, with smooth $L^2$ forcing and
satisfying
$$\frac d{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(x,t)|^2\,dx
  =2\int_{\mathbb R^3}u(x,t)\cdot f(x,t)\,dx,$$
develop a finite-time singularity, in the sense that
$\sup_x|\nabla u(x,t)|\to+\infty$ as $t\to T^-$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 35]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (T : ℝ) (u : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector) (p : VelocityVector → ℝ → ℝ)
      (f : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector),
      0 < T ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ (⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞) (Function.uncurry f) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T) ∧
      MemLp (Function.uncurry f) 2 (volume.restrict (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T)) ∧
      IsSmoothFiniteEnergySolution T u p f ∧
      Tendsto (gradientSup u) (𝓝[<] T) (𝓝 ⊤) := by
  sorry

/--
Elgindi's solved lower-regularity variant: there are $0<\alpha<1$, a divergence-free odd
$u_0\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb R^3)$, and $C>0$ with
$|\omega_0(x)|\le C/(|x|^\alpha+1)$, such that the unique odd
$C^{1,\alpha}_{x,t}$ solution of the unforced incompressible Euler equations on
$\mathbb R^3\times[0,1)$ has
$$\int_0^t\|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds\longrightarrow+\infty
  \quad\text{as }t\to1^-.$$
These solutions have infinite energy and do not satisfy the energy balance in `euler_equations`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 35]
theorem euler_equations.variants.elgindi :
    ∃ (α : ℝ≥0) (u₀ : VelocityVector → VelocityVector) (u : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector) (p : VelocityVector → ℝ → ℝ)
      (C : ℝ),
      0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧ 0 < C ∧
      IsC1AlphaOn α u₀ univ ∧
      (∀ x, divergence u₀ x = 0) ∧
      IsOddVelocity u₀ ∧
      (∀ x, ‖vorticity u₀ x‖ ≤ C / (‖x‖ ^ (α : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      IsC1AlphaFreeSolution α u₀ u p ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, IsOddVelocity (u · t)) ∧
      (∀ (v : VelocityVector → ℝ → VelocityVector) (q : VelocityVector → ℝ → ℝ),
        IsC1AlphaFreeSolution α u₀ v q →
        (∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, IsOddVelocity (v · t)) → v = u) ∧
      Tendsto (fun t ↦ ∫⁻ s in Ioc (0 : ℝ) t, vorticitySup u s) (𝓝[<] (1 : ℝ)) (𝓝 ⊤) := by
  sorry

end EulerEquations
modeling_decisions: The terse list entry is interpreted via the cited Euler-equations article and Elgindi's Question 1.1 as the finite-time blow-up question for smooth forced incompressible Euler flow on ℝ³, rather than for compressible flow or a torus.

The primary question quantifies a positive finite time T, velocity, pressure, and forcing; forcing is smooth and L² on ℝ³×[0,T], velocity is spatially L² at every t<T, and the differential energy balance is imposed on [0,T). Integrability of its RHS is explicit to avoid Mathlib's junk value for a nonintegrable Bochner integral.

Spatial gradient and vorticity suprema take values in ℝ≥0∞, and blow-up is convergence to ⊤ from the left. This faithfully permits genuinely unbounded spatial suprema without relying on real-supremum default values.
Spatial vectors use the Euclidean ℓ² structure on three coordinates. The norm of the Fréchet derivative is used for |∇u|; this is an equivalent standard matrix norm for the blow-up question.
The primary formulation uses ℝ³ (not the torus), permits smooth L² forcing as in Elgindi's Question 1.1, and requires pressure to be smooth as part of a classical smooth Euler solution.
For Elgindi's theorem, 0<α<1 is made explicit from the paper's Hölder-space convention and surrounding local well-posedness discussion.

The paper's global bounded Hölder norm is used for u₀. The evolving C^{1,α}_{x,t} condition is local on the half-open spacetime domain, so its Hölder constants need not remain uniform as t approaches the excluded blow-up time.
Elgindi oddness means component u_i is odd under reflection of coordinate i and even under reflection of either other coordinate, exactly as defined in the paper.
The 'unique local odd solution' clause asserts uniqueness of velocity among odd C^{1,α} Euler solutions with the same initial data. Pressure is not required to be unique because it has gauge freedom.
The Elgindi time integral is an extended nonnegative Lebesgue integral over (0,t]; changing endpoint inclusion does not alter the intended Lebesgue integral.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations

This file concerns finite-time singularity formation for the three-dimensional
incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R^3$. It also records Elgindi's solved
$C^{1,\alpha}$ variant.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Euler equations (fluid dynamics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_equations_%28fluid_dynamics%29)
- [T. M. Elgindi, *Finite-time singularity formation for $C^{1,\alpha}$ solutions to the
  incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R^3$*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04795)
-/

open ContDiff Filter InnerProductSpace MeasureTheory Set

namespace EulerEquations

abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- The divergence of a vector field on $\mathbb R^3$. -/
noncomputable def divergence (v : Space → Space) (x : Space) : ℝ :=
  (fderiv ℝ v x).trace ℝ Space

/-- The vorticity $\nabla\times v$ of a vector field on $\mathbb R^3$. -/
noncomputable def vorticity (v : Space → Space) (x : Space) : Space :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 ![
    (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)).ofLp 2 -
      (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1)).ofLp 1,
    (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1)).ofLp 0 -
      (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1)).ofLp 2,
    (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1)).ofLp 1 -
      (fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)).ofLp 0]

/-- Elgindi's notion of an odd vector field: its $i$th component is odd in $x_i$
and even in the other two coordinates. -/
def IsOdd (v : Space → Space) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i j : Fin 3) (x : Space),
    (v (WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j (-x.ofLp j)))).ofLp i =
      if i = j then -(v x).ofLp i else (v x).ofLp i

/-- A map is globally $C^{1,\alpha}$ on `s`: it is differentiable there, both it and
its derivative are bounded there, and its derivative is $\alpha$-Hölder on `s`. -/
def IsC1HolderOn {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : NNReal) (g : E → F) (s : Set E) : Prop :=
  DifferentiableOn ℝ g s ∧
    ∃ C₀ C₁ : ℝ, ∃ C₂ : NNReal,
      (∀ z ∈ s, ‖g z‖ ≤ C₀) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ s, ‖fderiv ℝ g z‖ ≤ C₁) ∧
      HolderOnWith C₂ α (fderiv ℝ g) s

/-- A map is $C^{1,\alpha}$ before time `T` if it is globally $C^{1,\alpha}$ in
space-time on every closed time interval strictly inside $[0,T)$. -/
def IsC1HolderBefore (α : NNReal) (g : Space × ℝ → Space) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ τ, 0 < τ → τ < T → IsC1HolderOn α g (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 τ)

/-- The incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R^3\times[0,T)$, with external
force `f`. Time derivatives are taken relative to the half-open time interval. -/
def IsEulerSolution (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (p : Space → ℝ → ℝ)
    (f : Space → ℝ → Space) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ x t, t ∈ Ico 0 T → DifferentiableWithinAt ℝ (u x) (Ico 0 T) t) ∧
  (∀ t, t ∈ Ico 0 T → Differentiable ℝ (u · t) ∧ Differentiable ℝ (p · t)) ∧
  (∀ x t, t ∈ Ico 0 T →
    derivWithin (u x) (Ico 0 T) t + fderiv ℝ (u · t) x (u x t) + gradient (p · t) x =
      f x t) ∧
  (∀ x t, t ∈ Ico 0 T → divergence (u · t) x = 0)

/-- The kinetic-energy balance for a forced Euler flow on $[0,T)$. This includes
finite kinetic energy and integrability of the work term at every time. -/
def HasEnergyBalance (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (f : Space → ℝ → Space) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 T,
    Integrable (fun x ↦ ‖u x t‖ ^ 2) ∧
    Integrable (fun x ↦ ⟪u x t, f x t⟫_ℝ) ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s ↦ ∫ x, ‖u x s‖ ^ 2)
      (2 * ∫ x, ⟪u x t, f x t⟫_ℝ) (Ico 0 T) t

/-- The spatial gradient of `u` becomes unbounded as time approaches `T` from below. -/
def HasGradientBlowup (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ τ, 0 < τ → τ < T → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x t, t ∈ Icc 0 τ →
    ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖ ≤ C) ∧
  Tendsto (fun t ↦ ⨆ x, ENNReal.ofReal ‖fderiv ℝ (u · t) x‖)
    (nhdsWithin T (Ico 0 T)) atTop

/-- The time integral of the spatial $L^\infty$ norm of the vorticity diverges as
time approaches `T` from below. -/
def HasVorticityIntegralBlowup (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Tendsto (fun t ↦ ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..t, ⨆ x, ‖vorticity (u · s) x‖)
    (nhdsWithin T (Ico 0 T)) atTop

/--
**Regularity of solutions of the Euler equations.** In the precise $\mathbb R^3$
formulation of Elgindi's Question 1.1, can a smooth, divergence-free solution of
$\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=f$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[0,T)$, with smooth
spacetime-$L^2$ force on $\mathbb R^3\times[0,T]$ and finite energy satisfying the
energy balance, have
$\lim_{t\uparrow T}\sup_x|\nabla u(x,t)|=+\infty$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 35]
theorem euler_equations :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ (T : ℝ) (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (p : Space → ℝ → ℝ)
        (f : Space → ℝ → Space),
        0 < T ∧
        ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry u) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
        ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry p) (univ ×ˢ Ico 0 T) ∧
        ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry f) (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T) ∧
        MemLp (Function.uncurry f) 2
          ((volume.prod volume).restrict (univ ×ˢ Icc 0 T)) ∧
        IsEulerSolution u p f T ∧ HasEnergyBalance u f T ∧ HasGradientBlowup u T := by
  sorry

/--
**Elgindi's $C^{1,\alpha}$ finite-time singularity theorem.** There are $\alpha>0$,
a divergence-free odd $u_0\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb R^3)$, and $C>0$ such that
$|\omega_0(x)|\le C/(|x|^\alpha+1)$. The unique local odd $C^{1,\alpha}$ solution
of the unforced incompressible Euler equations with initial value $u_0$, on
$[0,1)$, satisfies
$\lim_{t\uparrow1}\int_0^t\|\omega(s)\|_{L^\infty}\,ds=+\infty$.
This solution has infinite energy and does not satisfy the energy balance.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 35]
theorem euler_equations.variants.elgindi :
    ∃ (α : NNReal) (C : ℝ) (u₀ : Space → Space)
      (u : Space → ℝ → Space) (p : Space → ℝ → ℝ),
      0 < α ∧ 0 < C ∧
      IsC1HolderOn α u₀ univ ∧
      (∀ x, divergence u₀ x = 0) ∧ IsOdd u₀ ∧
      (∀ x, ‖vorticity u₀ x‖ ≤ C / (‖x‖ ^ (α : ℝ) + 1)) ∧
      ¬ Integrable (fun x ↦ ‖u₀ x‖ ^ 2) ∧
      IsC1HolderBefore α (Function.uncurry u) 1 ∧
      IsEulerSolution u p 0 1 ∧
      (∀ x, u x 0 = u₀ x) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, IsOdd (u · t)) ∧
      (∀ (v : Space → ℝ → Space) (q : Space → ℝ → ℝ),
        IsC1HolderBefore α (Function.uncurry v) 1 →
        IsEulerSolution v q 0 1 →
        (∀ x, v x 0 = u₀ x) →
        (∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, IsOdd (v · t)) →
        ∀ x t, t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1 → v x t = u x t) ∧
      HasVorticityIntegralBlowup u 1 ∧ ¬ HasEnergyBalance u 0 1 := by
  sorry
